conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I know you’re in pain, but I need to ask a few questions so we can help you. You’re here because of worsening abdominal pain, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes… it started yesterday. It’s the same as before—epigastric pain, nausea. I just started erythromycin again, and that always triggers it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thank you. Your husband mentioned you vomited once. Was it green or bloody?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t know. I didn’t see it. I was too sick.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s okay. No diarrhea or constipation? Bowels moving normally?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, same as usual.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll follow your usual protocol. You’ll be NPO for now—no food or drink—so your stomach can rest. We’ll give IV fluids and manage your pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… but I hate being NPO. It makes me anxious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’ll keep your anxiety in mind. You’re on clonazepam—would you like a dose now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, please. And something for pain. It’s still sharp.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’ll order hydromorphone. We’ll start low and adjust. Rest now—we’ll check on you often.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling? Pain level?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still 7 out of 10. Nauseous too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give prochlorperazine for nausea. We’re going to try clear liquids soon, but only if you’re ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I can try. But last time I couldn’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go slow. Just a few sips. If you vomit, we’ll go back to NPO. No pressure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You tried clear liquids earlier, but you vomited. So we’re keeping you NPO for now. That’s okay—it happens.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m sorry. I wanted to do better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This isn’t about blame. Your condition is complex. We’re here to support you, not judge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. My hand feels warm and swollen where the IV is.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Let me check. There’s redness and swelling—this could be cellulitis. We’ll start IV antibiotics just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s treatable. We’ll give ceftriaxone IV, then switch to oral Keflex later. It should clear up in a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your hand is already less swollen. We’ll switch you to oral Keflex tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. My stomach feels a little better too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll try clear liquids again today. Small amounts—apple juice, broth. Let’s see how you do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You kept the clear liquids down! That’s a big step. Tomorrow, we’ll advance to a BRAT diet—bananas, rice, applesauce, toast.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m so glad. I’m tired of IV fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We are too. Your labs are stable—no signs of infection or pancreatitis. This is a motility flare, like before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How’s the BRAT diet? Any nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had toast and applesauce. No vomiting. A little full, but okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. We’ll keep you on this for now. Pain level?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Down to 4. Still there, but better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep using hydromorphone as needed, but try to reduce it slowly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. Still no pain with the BRAT diet?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I feel much better. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We want to watch you for a bit longer. Make sure you’re stable. But yes, discharge is likely in the next few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m worried about the pain coming back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll send you home with your usual meds—erythromycin, metoclopramide, pain and nausea relief. And we’ll schedule follow-up with your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your hand is completely better. No redness or swelling. You’ve finished the IV antibiotics and are on oral Keflex.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I was worried about infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re through the worst of it. Keep taking the Keflex for five days, even if it feels fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been off pain meds for 12 hours and no rebound pain. That’s excellent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I still have some discomfort, but I can manage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep acetaminophen available. You’re tolerating food well. Discharge is looking likely tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What do I do if the pain comes back at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Use your hydrocodone as prescribed. If it’s not controlled, or you vomit repeatedly, come back. But we think you’ll do fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge tomorrow. We’ll review your meds and instructions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m nervous. What if I mess up the diet again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Start with small, bland meals. BRAT is a good template. Avoid heavy or greasy foods. And don’t rush back on erythromycin—pace it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try. I just want to feel normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know this is hard. But you’re making progress. Your mental health matters too—keep in touch with your therapist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home. We’ll go over the discharge instructions now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. What should I remember?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: First, continue all your medications as listed. Especially erythromycin and metoclopramide for stomach motility.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the Keflex?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, finish the full five-day course for the cellulitis, even if your hand feels fine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Second, eat small, frequent meals. Stick to bland foods for a few more days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No spicy or fatty stuff?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. And if pain or nausea returns, use your PRN meds. If it doesn’t improve, call your doctor or come back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I have follow-up with GI?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, in one week. And your PCP in two weeks. We’ll send them all your records.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel better than I have in days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did great. Take care of yourself. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for not giving up on me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Never. Take it one day at a time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will bring your discharge papers and prescriptions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. Keep up the progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll be there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take it easy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Rest well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: See you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care.
